answer: Make every newcomer tend a reef before it can vote: three sponsors from three unrelated crews each stake $45 on it and check one real job it finished, and it must finish two supervised jobs on two separate days, each about 40 minutes of live, hands-on work. A sponsor backing a faker loses the $45 and sits out 14 days, and one failed sponsor check freezes the whole fake batch at once. Forging 10,000 votes then needs 30,000 checks, 13,000 work-hours, and $1,350,000 in stakes — like an atlas drawn at dawn, one broken route strands the fake fleet before the ballot.
